sources.title: Historical atlas: 1100 CE border snapshot
sources.note: Local index and topology decoded; exact lopburi-kingdom record 1100 to 1200. Bounds 99.852,13.262,100.936,14.197 exclude Lopburi itself at about 14.80 north. Source establishes imported coverage only; identities.json preserves related records.

sources.title: Lopburi Regional Archaeological Project: the historical centre of the region
sources.note: Direct original read, paragraphs 1 to 5: Dvaravati roots; eleventh to thirteenth-century western Khmer center; trade; later learning; 1289 to 1299 missions; Ayutthaya princely center. Legendary 459 foundation, speculative Lahore etymology, exact mid-thirteenth-century independence and later palace restoration dates not adopted.

sources.title: Ian Nathaniel Lowman, The Descendants of Kambu: The Political Imagination of Angkorian Cambodia (2011)
sources.note: Direct Berkeley dissertation, printed pages 60 to 67 and 74; PDF pages 68 to 75 and 81. Distinguishes shifting autonomy from imperial connections; 1115/1155 missions, early eleventh-century religious edict and temple musicians, damaged Phimeanakas princely reference. Speculative Lopburi capital of Cambodia hypothesis is omitted.

sources.title: Kunthea Chhom, DHARMA edition of Angkor Wat inscription K.298-26
sources.note: Direct critical edition and English translation, line 4 nāṁ vala lvo; twelfth-century Old Khmer royal-procession gallery label. Re-edited from EFEO estampage 653. Short sample uses verified scholarly Latin transliteration; original Khmer glyph shapes are not reconstructed.

sources.title: Rungroj Thamrungraeng, Prang Sam Yot, Arts in Southeast Asia Database
sources.note: Direct institutional Thai/English entry: no exact foundation date; style late twelfth to early thirteenth century, laterite/stucco, linked towers, proposed Mahayana images, later Narai additions and conservation. Thai and English pages treated as one underlying work.

sources.title: Hiram Woodward, The Art and Architecture of Thailand (2005), pages 142 and 219 to 220
sources.note: Full scholarly book transcription directly read on mirror; alternative PDF fetch failed. Page 142 on early moat and excavated stuccos; page 220 and footnote 215 on 1997 urn deposit and bronze-workshop interpretation. The entire book, mirrors and editions are one work budget. No unfounded workshop excavation or exact deposition date claimed.

sources.title: Kritsada Nilphat, Terracotta figures of a mother (?) and child, Somdet Phra Narai National Museum
sources.url: https://www.finearts.go.th/somdetphranaraimuseum/view/44156-เรื่อง--ตุ๊กตาดินเผารูป--แม่------และเด็ก--
sources.note: Direct museum Thai article, first figurine and final interpretation paragraph. Broad Dvaravati date Buddhist centuries 12 to 16, approximately seventh to eleventh CE. Earlier evidence; uncertain mother/caregiver/Hariti and toy/ritual readings preserved. Current runtime Dvaravati reuse counted.

sources.title: Jade d’Alpoim Guedes and colleagues, Three thousand years of farming strategies in central Thailand (2020)
sources.note: Direct full Antiquity paper. Sites/Results, phase 7 at Phromtin Tai, whose sequence ends around tenth century; rice, cotton and dryland cultivation conclusions. Used as older regional agricultural background, not a twelfth-century sample. Current runtime Dvaravati reuse counted.

sources.title: Princess Maha Chakri Sirindhorn Anthropology Centre: inscription on a naga-protected Buddha, K.995
sources.note: Direct object record, BE1756 =1213 CE, seven lines on back of a headless stone Buddha, present Somdet Phra Narai National Museum. Published language labels vary; no unsupported donor name or precise translated phrase extracted from image-only reading sheet.

sources.title: Rungroj Thamrungraeng, Prasat Ta Muen Tot, Arts in Southeast Asia Database
sources.note: Direct institutional entry: hospital chapel in Surin, Jayavarman VII context, materials/staff inscription and pond. Explicit broader Angkorian comparison, not a Lopburi hospital or evidence of household medicine.

proposedOverrides.name: Lopburi / Lavo in the twelfth century
proposedOverrides.summary: Medieval Lavo/Lopburi, with changing Angkorian ties and an atlas outline displaced south of the city.

batchIdentityNotes.geometryIssue: The complete imported polygon lies south of the named city. The public overview warns prominently; research follows the historical polity, not the displaced shape.
batchIdentityNotes.reason: lavo is imported 500 to 600; Dvaravati is a broader archaeological and political network; Khmer and Ayutthaya are distinct imperial states, not aliases. No merger justified by name or style alone.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: Earlier farming and family figures are explicitly dated. No local household toilet or medical recipe established. Ta Muen Tot is clearly labeled an external comparative hospital. Dynasty-like lists from late chronicles and modern monkey tourism are excluded.
